name: Hauts-de-France
summary_text: Region research direction: worse than national — municipal practice of the far-right party in the Nord/Pas-de-Calais mining basin. Around thirty local associations accuse newly won far-right town halls of cancelling or hollowing out local Pride events while claiming to defend LGBT rights ("we are not fooled by this pinkwashing"); party MEPs have voted against conversion-therapy resolutions. Documented pattern across several communes, not one mayor's statement. Model-estimate residual (route 3, best-knowledge delta): large urban student scene around Lille vs rural voting patterns inland. National context from this record's sources: trans detainees in French prisons are placed by the gender on their identity documents (criminal procedure code D248), fall into a legal grey area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes — the national detention controller-general's office says transgender detainees are the group that "suffers the most" in detention; its 2021 Opinion covering all places of deprivation of liberty (based on ~40 referrals since 2010) finds serious violations persisting, with isolation, untrained staff and unimplemented 2016 depathologisation identified as the structural causes.

sources.title: The Plight Of Trans Women In Prison
sources.claim_summary: Investigative feature (Jan 2018) on transgender women in French prisons: by law, placement follows the gender on identity documents (criminal procedure code Article D248), so trans women legally marked male are held in all-male facilities — case of Paola, three days in a men's facility near Lille after transfer in 2014, shouted at and threatened by inmates; case of Kara B. held under notorious conditions after a 2016 Paris protest trial; the national detention controller-general (CGLPL) states transgender detainees are the group that "suffers the most" in prison.

National detention controller-general's Opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in all places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations persist across institutions (based on ~40 referrals since 2010 plus interviews and inspections); recommends that detained people choose the gender of their search officer and ward, no isolation because of trans identity, no dedicated trans-only wards, and ongoing hormone/medical care; extends to intersex and non-binary people; notes the 2016 depathologising law has not been translated into prison rules.

International anti-torture body interview with the French national detention mechanism (May 2023) about its 2021 Opinion: trans persons in detention face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; research found a lack of data on trans detainees' numbers and locations, almost no staff training, and no guidance implementing the 2016 law; central recommendation is that detaining authorities ask people what they require and respond; five dedicated inspection visits were carried out across regions and institution types.
